title: Ratio and Proportion (KS3)
subject: Maths
strapline: Comparing quantities and sharing amounts fairly.
facts: A ratio compares two or more quantities, written with a colon: 2:3.
Simplify a ratio by dividing all parts by their highest common factor: 4:6 = 2:3.
To share an amount in a ratio, add the parts to find the total number of parts, then find the value of one part.
Share £20 in the ratio 2:3 → 5 parts, so one part = £4, giving £8 and £12.
Direct proportion: as one quantity increases, the other increases at the same rate.
The unitary method: find the value of one item first, then scale up.
Ratios have no units and are usually written in their simplest whole-number form.

quick_quiz.q: If 3 pens cost £1.50, what does 1 pen cost?

teacher_tips: Add the parts first — the most common sharing error is skipping this.
Use the unitary method consistently for proportion problems.
Bar models make "parts of a whole" visible.
